correctness.rationale: Incidence filtration determines the complete relevant Kneser adjacency spectrum; Laplacian Rayleigh inequality isolates the only possible three-vertex minimum cut side. The uniform ratio t/d<=3/10 and degree/order bounds establish strict exclusion of every component of size >=4. A second use of the spectral inequality proves three-vertex deletion connectivity, enabling sharp constructions; exact counting of P3 and K3 triples gives the minimum-cut census. The proof handles all k>=3 and n>=3k-1. Finite verifier separately corroborates two base orders and numeric inequalities.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Super cyclic edge-connectivity constrains cuts separating cycles, while a minimal triple at n=3k-1 is a path and acyclic; neither is a special case of the other invariant. For n>=3k, cyclic cuts are relevant because triangles exist; the accessible abstract does not establish the exhaustive lambda3 classification or cut counts, but the inaccessible proof remains a genuine residual risk. The theorem does not claim a new ordinary restricted or cyclic connectivity value.

value.rationale: The third restricted edge-connectivity is a motivated graph-network reliability invariant. Exact all-higher-rank cut values, super-restricted rigidity, complete numbers of optimal failures and the sharp transition from acyclic paths to triangles at n=3k give structural information rather than merely a computational table. The complement of the isolated triple is provably connected; counts concern actual edge-cut failure sets.
